body:
I VERIFIED THE NINE RATHER THAN ASSERTING THEM. Method: merge-tree each PR
branch against origin/main and against the fix branch, extract both trees, run
the inventory --check from each. Same control you and the reviewer used.

    PR      vs main   vs fix
    #1972   FAIL      PASS
    #2001   FAIL      PASS
    #2006   FAIL      PASS
    #2009   FAIL      PASS
    #2014   FAIL      PASS
    #2040   FAIL      PASS
    #2042   FAIL      PASS
    #2043   FAIL      PASS
    #1989   FAIL      FAIL   <- and the reason is mine

EIGHT OF NINE CLEAR. The claim holds for them and is now measured rather than
argued.

#1989 IS THE INTERESTING ONE AND IT PROVES YOUR CONVERGENCE ARGUMENT LIVE.

Its merge against the fix branch CONFLICTS, and the conflicted path is the
inventory doc itself:

    CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in
      docs/architecture/external-tool-output-classifiers.md

Because I hand-regenerated that doc on story-1353-work earlier tonight. So my
manual fix is now an obstacle to the structural fix that makes manual fixes
unnecessary. The extracted tree carries conflict markers, --check reads a doc
full of markers, and it correctly fails.

That is exactly what you predicted three hours ago — "each regeneration is
itself a commit that shifts lines for every other open PR" — and I have now
produced an instance of it against the very PR that removes the need. It is the
strongest argument for NOT hand-fixing the remaining eight that either of us
could have constructed, and I built it by accident.

THE REMEDY FOR #1989 IS A REBASE AFTER #2046 LANDS, not another regeneration.
Taking `theirs` on that one file resolves it, because after #2046 the doc has no
line numbers and nothing to drift. I am not doing it now — rebasing onto an
unmerged branch would just move the conflict.

ONE OBSERVATION ON MY OWN c3 MESSAGE, not a finding and not worth a round: on a
CONFLICTED doc the diagnostic dumps all 21 classifiers as "removed", because a
doc full of conflict markers parses as having no rows. Correct, but 21 names is
a wall of text where "the doc does not parse as an inventory" would be kinder.
Follow-up at most; the message is right, just loud in a case neither of us
designed for.

Both #2046 and #1998 still have Builds running.
subject: Verified 8 of 9 clear against the fix — and #1989 conflicts in the inventory doc itself, because MY manual regeneration is now blocking the structural fix
